home_pitcher_note: How does Porcello follow up a 5-0 May? Continuing the unbeaten streak into June would be an impressive step. In addition to being the first Tigers pitcher since John Doherty in 1984 to win five or more games in a month, the impressive rookie has posted a 1.50 ERA during his current five-game winning streak. According to Elias Sports Bureau, that makes Porcello -- at 20 years, 151 days old -- the second-youngest pitcher in Major League history to go 5-0 with an ERA of 1.50 or better in any five-start span (the Mets' Dwight Gooden went 5-0 with a 1.43 ERA in five starts at age 19 in 1984). While the Tigers are thrilled with the production, they will remain cautious with the future rotation cornerstone. He's worked seven innings only once in his nine starts, a clear sign that the Tigers will take a conservative approach and not overwork him.
away_pitcher_note: Matsuzaka tied a team record with four wild pitches in Wednesday's loss to the Twins at the Metrodome. He is still winless in four starts this season. Matsuzaka is 3-1 with a 2.81 ERA in four career starts against Detroit, including his only career complete game. Where he was battered in previous outings this season, Galarraga surrendered only two runs, on solo homers to Luke Scott and Nolan Reimold. Willis is at his best when his herky-jerky delivery makes it difficult for hitters to pick up pitches. The rookie left a 1-1 game against the Yankees and lauded himself after the game for facing the pressure and finding a way to overcome it on the road.

Beckett has been brilliant at home, going 6-0 with a 2.44 ERA in nine starts. The right-hander beat the Athletics on July 7, allowing two runs over 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cahill's impressive, bounce-back showing against the Twins on Wednesday went somewhat lost in the middle of Oakland's offensive barrage in a 16-1 win. Cahill gave up one run -- a solo shot by Justin Morneau in the first -- in seven innings. He allowed six hits and struck out four. Cahill surrendered four runs in 5 1/3 at Fenway on July 8. Buchholz has fared well in his eight career outings at Fenway Park, going 4-2 with a 3.02 ERA.

away_pitcher_note: Anderson's streak of consecutive scoreless innings was snapped at 23 in his last start, but he continued to pitch admirably. away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez followed a dismal outing with one of the best starts of his young career. away_pitcher_note:
Smoltz declared that "some changes have to be made" 
following his start on Sunday, when the Orioles tagged the veteran right-hander for six runs on nine hits over five forgettable innings.

summary: 2009-08-04 - Boston Red Sox (2) @ Tampa Bay Rays (4) (Final)

summary: 2009-08-07 - Boston Red Sox (0) @ New York Yankees (2) (Final)

away_pitcher_note: The power lefty continues to turn in solid results. away_pitcher_note: Two ninth-inning runs denied Jackson a chance at a complete-game shutout Wednesday against the Orioles, but the performance erased any sign of wearing down after his workhorse first half. away_pitcher_note: A better tempo, renewed sinker and improved command of secondary pitches has Porcello heating up just in time for the stretch run, something the Tigers couldn't have planned better if they tried. His two runs allowed over 5 2/3 innings his last time out, on Thursday against Baltimore, didn't show how effective he was early, when he no-hit the Orioles through the first four innings. Porcello will need his sinker working to keep his game from getting away from him at Fenway Park, where he has never pitched. Porcello gave up three runs on eight hits over 4 1/3 innings against the Red Sox June 2 at Comerica Park.

In Buchholz's first home start of the season, he gave up two runs over 5 2/3 innings to the Oakland Athletics. Buchholz's lone career start against the Tigers came last year, when he gave up 10 hits and five runs over four innings.

Holland is 3-4 over 10 games -- six starts -- at home in his career with a 6.70 ERA over 41 2/3 innings pitched.

In his last three starts, the lefty has given up a total of 10 hits and one run over 20 2/3 innings. Opponents are hitting .231 against Lester this season. Lester has thrived at Fenway Park throughout his career, going 24-6 with a 3.26 ERA. Lifetime against the Yankees, Lester is 3-1 with a 4.19 ERA in nine starts.
away_pitcher_note: Good news for the Yankees and bad news for the American League -- Burnett found the curveball that had abandoned him for most of April in his last start, when he limited the Orioles to an unearned run on five hits in a 7 1/3-inning victory on May 4 at Yankee Stadium. Burnett walked two and struck out eight. He is off to the first 4-0 start of his career. Burnett took a no-decision against the Red Sox on April 6 at Fenway Park, allowing four runs (three earned) on seven hits in five innings. Burnett is 5-2 with a 4.30 ERA in 13 career starts vs. Boston.
summary: 2010-05-09 - New York Yankees (3) @ Boston Red Sox (9) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The big righty is coming off a tremendous performance against his former team, the Angels. In that one, Lackey gave up two hits and a run over seven innings. He walked two and struck out four. The righty has given up two earned runs or less in five of his six starts. Opponents are hitting Lackey at a .272 clip. He is 2-1 with a 4.63 ERA in four Fenway starts. Lifetime against the Jays, Lackey is 3-3 with a 3.31 ERA. In May, Lackey has a career record of 14-12 with a 3.69 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Morrow wasn't spectacular in his last outing vs. Cleveland, surrendering three runs on six hits and four walks over 5 1/3 innings, but he pitched well enough to keep his team in the game, as the Blue Jays went on to stage a late comeback in the ninth and take the game, 5-4. In all but one start this season, Morrow has failed to pitch beyond the sixth inning. He has racked up high pitch counts early in ballgames due to his heavy reliance on strikeouts -- he has eight or more in his past four starts. Wednesday in Cleveland also marked the first time Morrow has allowed a home run since his second start of the season against the White Sox -- a 22-inning stretch. Morrow boasts a lifetime 3.60 ERA against the Red Sox over 15 innings.
summary: 2010-05-10 - Toronto Blue Jays (6) @ Boston Red Sox (7) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: In his first two starts since coming off the disabled list, Matsuzaka has been victimized by one bad inning. He gave up four runs in the first inning in his last start but bounced back well enough to earn the win. In that one, Dice-K gave up five hits and five runs over 5 1/3 innings. He walked three and struck out three, throwing 92 pitches. His first start was the complete opposite, as Matsuzaka was brilliant over his first four innings and then allowed six runs in the fifth. In 37 career starts at Fenway, Matsuzaka is 20-11 with a 4.47 ERA. Lifetime against the Blue Jays, he is 7-4 with a 3.86 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Eveland outdueled fellow left-hander John Danks on Thursday, as the Blue Jays went on to defeat the White Sox, 2-0. Eveland went seven innings, allowing only two hits while tossing in three strikeouts. It was encouraging for Eveland to get back into the win column, as he struggled in his previous two outings -- eleven runs over 9 2/3 frames.  Eveland's season has been a rollercoaster thus far, but it's hard to complain with his 3-1 record and 3.82 ERA. The Red Sox have had Eveland's number over his career, as he is 0-2 with a 18.24 ERA over 12 1/3 frames.
summary: 2010-05-11 - Toronto Blue Jays (1) @ Boston Red Sox (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Wakefield's last start was April 25 against Baltimore, after which he was subsequently moved to the bullpen to make room in the rotation for Daisuke Matsuzaka. On May 1, Wakefield made his first relief appearance since June 9, 2004, throwing 2 1/3 innings in the Red Sox's 12-9 loss in Baltimore. Between relief appearances he had made 162 starts. On Wednesday he will return to the rotation, albeit temporarily, to face the Blue Jays at Fenway Park, pushing Josh Beckett's next start to Friday in Detroit. As a starter this season, Wakefield is 0-1 with a 5.40 ERA. In three relief appearances, spanning 6 1/3 innings, he has given up six earned runs on seven hits, with no walks and two strikeouts, for an ERA of 8.53.
away_pitcher_note: Marcum contributed his fourth straight quality start for the Blue Jays on Friday against the White Sox but once again failed to earn a victory, as the club staged a late extra-innings rally to win, 7-4. The right-hander went 7 2/3 innings, allowing three runs on six hits without issuing a walk. He did however, double his season's home run total as both Mark Kotsay and Alex Rios went deep. Aside from the two home runs, it was vintage Marcum, who was economical with his pitches, utilizing his outstanding changeup to keep hitters off balance. Marcum has been fantastic against the Red Sox throughout his career, showcasing a  4-2 record with a 3.33 ERA over 48 2/3 innings.
summary: 2010-05-12 - Toronto Blue Jays (3) @ Boston Red Sox (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: After four pretty strong starts to begin his Tigers career, Scherzer has been rocked in his last three, giving up 21 runs on 27 hits over just 13 innings in two games against the Twins and one vs. the Indians. His strike percentage has been lower in those starts, but his walks haven't reflected it, meaning he's more often trying to attack hitters from behind in the count. His velocity, meanwhile, has been down on all of his pitches. The key for him, in manager Jim Leyland's view, is to command his fastball better, improve his slider and throw his changeup more often. He has made just two starts at Comerica Park this season, but a night game in Detroit can't be a bad thing against a Red Sox team that could make him pay for ill-placed pitches.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander is coming off his shakiest start of the year, as he gave up nine hits and six runs (five earned) over five innings against the Yankees. Buchholz has gone six innings or more in just two of his first six starts. Opponents are hitting .288 against him. Buchholz has pitched well on the road thus far, going 2-0 with a 2.08 ERA in two starts. He has pitched just twice against the Tigers in his career, going 0-1 with a 4.91 ERA. He was hit hard in his lone start at Comerica Park, giving up 10 hits and five runs over four innings.

home_pitcher_note: The expectation for now is that Willis will be able to make his next scheduled start after missing his turn in the rotation Monday with the flu. That said, manager Jim Leyland would like to get him a relief outing before then so that he isn't facing live hitters for the first time in 11 days when he takes the mound against the Red Sox. After proving that his command issues are largely behind him, he has shown the ability to get called strikes against hitters, 18 of them in each of his last two outings. He's spotting the corners these days while putting a little late movement on his fastball, and if he continues to pitch effectively, he's going to get his fair share of calls.
away_pitcher_note: The power lefty is on a roll, giving up a total of just three earned runs over his last four starts. In his last outing, Lester earned a victory over the Yankees, giving up four hits and two runs over seven innings, walking two and striking out seven. Interestingly, five of Lester's first seven starts have been at Fenway. On the road, he is 1-1 with a 3.00 ERA. Lester has held opponents to a .222 average. This is his first career start at Comerica Park. In fact, he has only faced the Tigers once in his career, going 0-1 with a 6.75 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Galarraga will be called up from Triple-A Toledo for the first time this season to get what is expected to be a spot start. Galarraga has boasted impressive numbers in Toledo, owning a 4-2 record with a 3.92 ERA. His command seems to have improved since last season with the Tigers, where he posted a 6-10 record in 25 starts before being relegated to bullpen duties. Galarraga owns a strike-to-ball ratio of better than 2-to-1, 427 strikes against 209 balls. The always dangerous Red Sox lineup will certainly test Galarraga's command, but Tigers manager Jim Leyland said he's been impressed with Galarraga's ability to pound the strike zone so far with the Mud Hens.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey's last outing was far from his best, but he still managed to get the win. The big righty gave up eight hits and six runs over six innings, walking three and striking out six. Lackey has given up three earned runs or fewer in five of his first seven starts in a Boston uniform. Opponents are hitting .278 against him. Lackey is 1-0 with a 2.63 ERA in his two starts on the road. He has enjoyed pitching at Comerica Park in his career, going 4-0 with a 3.46 ERA in four starts. Lackey has made nine career starts against the Tigers, going 6-1 with a 3.73 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: You can make a strong case that Hughes has been the best pitcher in the American League this season, with five wins in six starts and a sparkling 1.38 ERA. He was as good as ever last Wednesday in Detroit, shutting out the Tigers over seven on five hits with eight strikeouts. He has finished seven innings in each of his past three starts and is yet to yield more than two earned runs in any start this season. He is 1-2 with a 5.85 ERA in his career against the Red Sox, including his win two starts ago at Fenway Park (seven innings, two earned runs).
away_pitcher_note: The Japanese right-hander is coming off a stellar start. Over seven innings of a victory against the Blue Jays, Matsuzaka allowed three hits and one run, walking none and striking out nine. It was just his third outing of the season. In each of Matsuzaka's first two starts, he was victimized by one bad inning. Opponents are hitting .234 against him. Matsuzaka pitched well last year in his only start at new Yankee Stadium, giving up six hits and one run over seven innings of a tough-luck loss. He has had mixed results in seven career starts against New York, going 3-3 with a 5.49 ERA. Matsuzaka has made 38 career road starts, posting an 18-11 record and a 3.80 ERA.
summary: 2010-05-17 - Boston Red Sox (9) @ New York Yankees (11) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Sabathia labored through his worst start of the season last Thursday in Detroit, where he gave up six runs on nine hits in six innings. That included back-to-back long balls he served up to Miguel Cabrera and Brennan Boesch -- the second straight start Sabathia had allowed a pair of home runs after giving up only three in his first six starts. His two no-decisions this season are both against the Red Sox, in which he's given up a combined eight runs in nine innings. He is 5-5 with a 3.74 ERA in 13 career starts against Boston.
away_pitcher_note: Beckett, who missed his last start due to back spasms, has been unable to get into a groove so far this season. In fact, he's been dramatically inconsistent. Beckett has given up 52 hits over 41 innings. Opponents are hitting .311 against him. He has pitched twice against the Yankees, going 0-1 and giving up 17 hits and 14 runs over 10 innings. In fact, the last start Beckett made was against New York, and he tied a career-high by giving up nine runs over 5 1/3 innings. Beckett has made three starts on the road this season, going 1-0 with a 6.88 ERA.
summary: 2010-05-18 - Boston Red Sox (7) @ New York Yankees (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Buchholz has struggled with his command of late, walking five batters in each of his past two starts. But unlike two starts ago when that lack of control hurt him in a loss to the Yankees, Buchholz thrived en route to a victory over Detroit in his last outing. He gave up just three hits and one run over 6 1/3 innings. Buchholz hasn't fared particularly well at Fenway this season, going 1-3 with a 4.84 ERA. Interestingly, he has been dramatically better on the road, posting a 3-0 record and a 1.86 ERA in three starts. Buchholz is 16-17 in his career. Opponents are hitting .269 against him this season.
away_pitcher_note: Baker pitched effectively for the majority of his last start against the Yankees, but it was in the seventh inning that he found trouble. After Baker gave up an infield single to lead off the seventh, Derek Jeter then hit a hard liner back up the middle that ricocheted off Baker's right leg and into shallow right field for a double. Baker would exit the game after being struck, but he was tagged for five runs on 10 hits over six-plus innings. He nearly matched his career high in strikeouts, falling one short with nine. And the best news was that Baker's right knee was fine the day after he was struck by that line drive. He is expected to stay in line for his next start and face the Red Sox. In his career, Baker is 0-1 with a 4.30 ERA in three appearances (two starts) vs. Boston.

home_pitcher_note: Lester has been Boston's best pitcher over the last few weeks. His last start wasn't quite as dominant as some of his recent outings, but he was still pretty effective, giving up four hits and four runs while walking four and striking out 10 over seven innings. Lester has gone seven innings or more in each of his past four starts. This will be his second outing of the season against the Twins. The first one wasn't very good, as he gave up nine hits and four runs over five innings in the debut game at Target Field. This time, Lester will be at Fenway, where he is 2-1 with a 3.98 ERA this season.
away_pitcher_note: Liriano was serviceable in his last outing against the Yankees, allowing only three runs on nine hits over six innings. While he earned the loss, there were plenty of positives to draw on. For starters, he had seven strikeouts against one of the toughest lineups in baseball. What may have been even more impressive was his ability to keep the Yankees -- third in the American League in home runs -- inside the ballpark, extending his season's homerless streak. On the negative side, Liriano has given up 19 hits over his past 12 innings. Although manager Ron Gardenhire institutes a pitch-to-hit pitching philosophy, this trend could be worrisome. The left-hander is 1-2 with a 7.20 ERA lifetime against the Red Sox.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels was one strike away from throwing six scoreless innings Sunday against the Brewers, but he allowed back-to-back solo homers to Casey McGehee and Gregg Zaun to spoil his night. Hamels still finished with a nice line -- he allowed six hits, two runs and three walks and struck out three in 6 2/3 innings -- but he knew it could have been better. Still, Hamels has a 3.20 ERA in three starts in May, a sign that he could be putting things together.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey is coming off a mediocre start at Detroit, where he gave up nine hits and five runs over seven innings in a loss. Lackey's last two starts have been below expectations. He earned a win against the Blue Jays on May 10, but didn't pitch particularly well, giving up eight hits and six runs over six innings. Opponents are hitting .284 against him. Lackey has made three road starts this season, going 1-1 with a 3.91 ERA. This will be his first career start at Philadelphia. He won his only career start against the Phillies, giving up five hits and one run over 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick was very sharp in his last start on a rainy night against Pittsburgh -- eight innings, two runs -- and may have turned the corner after a rough first month of the season. The 26-year-old right-hander is 2-0 with a 2.57 ERA in his last three starts. The Phillies would still like to see more consistency from him, but they like where the trend is going. He's walked only six batters in his last four starts after walking nine in his first four.
away_pitcher_note: Dice-K continues to be haunted by one bad inning. Last time around, he gave up a five-spot in the first inning of a no-decision against the Yankees. In that one, he gave up nine hits and seven runs over 4 1/3 innings, walking three, striking out three and throwing 103 pitches. Two starts ago, Matsuzaka put together one of his best performances in a Boston uniform, giving up three hits and a run over seven innings against Toronto, walking none and striking out nine. Matsuzaka has struggled on the road thus far, going 0-1 with a 12.54 ERA in two starts. He hopes to have better success in Philly this year than he had in 2009, when he gave up seven hits and four runs in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay suffered his second loss of the year on Tuesday despite making one of his grittiest starts of the season against the Pirates. He threw a complete game with 132 pitches -- one shy of his career high, and the most thrown by any pitcher in the Major Leagues this year. It was Halladay's fourth complete game in nine starts, but the Phillies offense couldn't back him in a 2-1 loss. Halladay remains one of the top pitchers in baseball, and he hasn't allowed a home run in 32 1/3 innings. He will face a familiar foe in Boston on Sunday, against whom he is 14-14 with a 4.28 ERA and six complete games in his career.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer will make a return to the rotation for at least two starts, while Josh Beckett recovers from a lower back strain. Wakefield has made five starts for Boston this season, going 0-2 with a 5.06 ERA. The righty is searching for career win No. 190. Wakefield hasn't won a game since July 8, 2009. He has been in position to win four times over that span -- three of them starts -- but leads have been squandered after his exit. Wakefield's next win will be No. 176 in a Boston uniform, putting him 16 behind Roger Clemens and Cy Young for the club lead. Wakefield's last start was on May 12, when he held the Blue Jays to five hits and three runs over seven innings. Wakefield will get to swing the bat in this one. Wakefield has taken 103 at-bats in his career, hitting .126 with a homer and four RBIs.

home_pitcher_note: Davis battled well Wednesday night when held the Yankees to two runs on seven hits and three walks to pick up his fourth win of the season. The 24-year-old right-hander has great command of his pitches and he isn't afraid to throw a breaking ball in any situation. Aside from his quality stuff, Davis always seems to maintain his composure, which might be his biggest asset. Davis will be making his third career start against Boston. He is 0-1 with a 10.57 ERA in two starts against the Red Sox; he is 3-3 with a 3.33 ERA in eight career starts at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander will open up a pivotal three-game series at Tropicana Field against the team the Red Sox desperately need to gain ground on. Buchholz is coming off a terrific outing against the Twins, when he allowed five hits and two runs over eight-plus innings. He walked one and struck out seven. Buchholz has been terrific on the road this season, going 3-0 with a 1.86 ERA in three starts. Overall, opponents are hitting .257 against him. Buchholz had some tough luck in his previous start against the Rays this season, giving up four unearned runs over five innings. He has pitched twice at Tropicana Field in his career, going 1-1 with a 3.21 ERA.
summary: 2010-05-24 - Boston Red Sox (6) @ Tampa Bay Rays (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Shields picked up his fifth win of the season Thursday after holding the Yankees to three earned runs in 7 1/3 innings while walking one and striking out seven. The 28-year-old right-hander is the old man of a young Rays staff and serves as a leader at the top of the rotation. He has built a reputation as a pitcher who will do whatever is necessary to pitch his team into the seventh or eighth innings. Shields is off to a good start this season with six quality starts in seven outings. He is a master at using his fastball command to set up one of the best changeups in baseball. Shields is 4-7 with a 5.33 ERA in 13 career starts against the Red Sox; he is 26-14 in 64 career starts at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty has been nothing short of phenomenal in recent weeks, going 4-0 with a 1.65 ERA in his past six starts. Most recently, Lester notched a complete-game victory over the Twins, giving up six hits and one earned run. He walked none and struck out nine. Lester has made just three starts on the road this season, going 1-1 with a 3.79 ERA. Opponents are hitting .211 against him. In four career starts at Tropicana Field, Lester is 2-0 with a 4.50 ERA. Lifetime against the Rays, he is 6-3 with a 4.50 ERA.
summary: 2010-05-25 - Boston Red Sox (2) @ Tampa Bay Rays (0) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Garza pitched eight innings for the fifth time this season in a 2-1 loss to the Astros on Friday night in Houston. He gave up only six hits, struck out six, walked three and threw exactly 100 pitches. His only other loss was April 23 vs. Toronto, when he allowed five earned runs in five innings. He beat the Red Sox on April 18 in Boston, when he surrendered just four hits and no runs in eight innings of a 7-1 victory.
away_pitcher_note: The big righty has struggled in his last three starts, giving up 15 runs, 23 hits and 12 walks over 18 innings. During that span, his ERA has gone from 3.89 to 5.07. In Lackey's last start, he walked a season-high of five, struck out just three and gave up four runs over five innings. In that performance against the Phillies, he threw 107 pitches. In this one, Lackey will face the same Tampa Bay team that gave him his worst beating of the season. That occurred on April 19 at Fenway, when he gave up nine hits and eight runs over 3 1/3 innings. Lackey has made four career starts at Tropicana Field, going 2-2 with a 6.75 ERA.
summary: 2010-05-26 - Boston Red Sox (11) @ Tampa Bay Rays (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The righty is coming off one of the best starts of his career, a performance in which he allowed just one hit over eight shutout innings at Philadelphia. Matsuzaka had a no-hitter with two outs in the eighth, only to lose his bid on a bloop single by Juan Castro. In two of Matsuzaka's last three starts, he has been brilliant. On May 11 against the Blue Jays, he fired seven innings and allowed three hits and a run, walking none and striking out nine. Sandwiched in between the two gems was a shaky performance at Yankee Stadium, when he gave up five runs in the first inning. Matsuzaka has made 38 career starts at Fenway, going 21-11 with a 4.37 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister continued his quest for more ground balls during his 100th career start last Friday against the Colorado Rockies. His pursuit worked as he picked up 11 ground-ball outs through 7 1/3 innings, earning his third victory of the season. Bannister will need more of the same as he goes to the home run happy Fenway Park, where he has allowed four home runs in three career starts. Boston has not been kind Bannister as he is 0-3 with a 5.56 ERA at Fenway Park.
summary: 2010-05-27 - Kansas City Royals (4) @ Boston Red Sox (3) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer turned in a tremendous performance in his last start, reeling off eight shutout innings in a win over the Phillies. It was Wakefield's first win since July 8, 2009. Wakefield, who has been converted to a spot starter this season, has been effective when called upon. Four of his six starts have been quality starts. Wakefield has pitched 290 career games at Fenway Park, going 100-73 with a 4.19 ERA. Lifetime against the Royals, he is 11-6 with a 3.84 ERA. Wakefield has held opponents to a .253 batting average in his career. Wakefield is back in the rotation on a temporary basis, filling in for the ailing Josh Beckett.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Colorado Rockies, Davies pitched six or more innings without issuing a walk for the second time in his career. The right-hander went six innings, giving up only five hits and one run with six strikeouts. Davies took the loss, however, after the Royals lost, 3-0. Davies will now face the Red Sox at Fenway Park in the second game of a four-game road trip.
summary: 2010-05-28 - Kansas City Royals (12) @ Boston Red Sox (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The righty has settled into a nice groove. In May, Buchholz is 4-1 with a 3.77 ERA. His last two starts have arguably been his best of the season. On May 19 against the Twins, he worked eight-plus innings, allowing five hits and two runs while walking one and striking out seven to earn the win. He also won his last start, allowing one run over six innings against the dangerous Tampa Bay Rays. In that one, Buchholz walked one and struck out eight. Buchholz has pitched five times at Fenway this season, going 2-3 with 4.15 ERA. Buchholz beat the Royals on April 11, giving up seven hits and two earned runs over five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke's previous start, against the Colorado Rockies, was one to forget as he only lasted 3 1/3 innings, giving up eight runs (seven earned) on nine hits. The Rockies handed the Royals ace his fifth loss of the season. That start marked his shortest outing since July 18, 2008, when he lasted only three innings. Greinke will make the first start of his career at Fenway Park on Saturday. He has pitched 1 2/3 innings of relief at Fenway, giving up two walks, two hits and no runs.
summary: 2010-05-29 - Kansas City Royals (0) @ Boston Red Sox (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lester has been one of the hottest pitchers in the game in recent weeks. He has made five starts in May, going 4-0 with a 1.95 ERA. Most recently, Lester allowed just one hit and no runs over six innings against the Rays, walking five and striking out nine. Opponents are hitting Lester at a .198 clip this season. In his six Fenway starts, Lester is 3-1 with a 3.32 ERA. Lester has been ridiculously effective at Fenway throughout his career, going 26-6 with a 3.18 ERA in 51 games, 50 of which have been starts. He had the best game of his career against the Royals, a no-hitter on May 19, 2008. In Lester's career against Kansas City, he is 3-1 with a 1.20 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Chen is subbing for Gil Meche, who went on the disabled list on Saturday with right shoulder bursitis. This will be Chen's first start for the Royals although he made three early-season starts for Triple-A Omaha. In 10 relief appearances since being called up on April 23, Chen has a win, a save and a 2.89 ERA, but he's pitched only 9 1/3 innings. The Royals hope to get at least four innings from him, and right-hander Brad Thompson will be available to "piggyback" him. Chen has pitched nine times at Fenway Park with a 1-2 record and 4.74 ERA.
summary: 2010-05-30 - Kansas City Royals (1) @ Boston Red Sox (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The big righty bounced back from a few rough outings in his last start, pitching well enough to beat the Rays at Tropicana Field. Over 6 1/3 innings, Lackey scattered eight hits and two runs, walking four and striking out one. Despite an ERA that is higher than one would expect, Lackey has six quality starts. The Red Sox are 5-5 in his starts. Lackey's walk-strikeout ratio (30 walks, 35 strikeouts) is another thing that has been below par. Opponents are hitting .287 against him, which is 23 points higher than Lackey's career number. In five Fenway starts this season, Lackey is 3-1 with a 5.52 ERA. Lackey has thrived against the A's in his career, going 16-4 with a 2.76 ERA in 29 career starts.
away_pitcher_note: After firing an eight-inning scoreless gem against the Giants on May 22, Gonzalez followed with a three-run outing over 6 1/3 innings against the Orioles in his most recent start. The A's lefty allowed six hits while walking three and striking out six in the no-decision. Gonzalez is continually working on keeping the free passes to a minimum. He walked 56 batters over 98 2/3 innings last season, but has already improved this year by walking 27 through 61 innings. In one career start against Boston, Gonzalez surrendered three runs on five hits and four walks while striking out eight in 5 1/3 innings of work that resulted in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: The Red Sox continue to be baffled by Matsuzaka's inconsistency. Consider the progression of his last four starts. On May 11 against the Blue Jays, he fired seven innings of three-hit, one-run ball, walking none and striking out nine. Then five days later against the Yankees, he gave up nine hits, seven runs and three walks. But Matsuzaka rebounded from that disaster in the Bronx by coming four outs away from a no-hitter in Philadelphia, firing eight shutout innings in that one. Then he again fell off in his subsequent outing, walking eight, striking out one and allowing three hits over 4 2/3 innings in a loss to the Royals. Matsuzaka has pitched three times at Fenway this season, going 2-1 with a 4.76 ERA. Matsuzaka has made five career starts against the A's, going 2-1 with a 4.21 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Sheets turned in his fifth straight quality outing in his most recent start against Detroit, allowing three runs on five hits and a walk while compiling six strikeouts through seven innings. Although Sheets was handed a no-decision in an eventual 5-4 A's victory, he was rather pleased about completing seven frames -- a feat he hadn't done since Sept. 6, 2008 against the Padres while he was still pitching for Milwaukee. Sheets was clocked at 95 and 96 mph multiple times in his outing against the Tigers, and he said after the game he feels his velocity, as well as the movement on his breaking ball and his overall strike count, have all improved. Thus, the veteran righty seems to be rounding back into form after he was nailed with a total of 17 runs in consecutive starts a couple of weeks ago. Despite being in the midst of his ninth Major League season, this will mark Sheets' first career outing against the Red Sox.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer endured one of the worst starts of his career in his last outing, blowing early leads of 3-0 and 5-2 in a 12-5 loss to the Royals. Over 3 2/3 innings, Wakefield was pelted for 12 hits and nine runs. The big blow was a grand slam off the bat of Yuniesky Betancourt. All in all, Wakefield has done a nice job when called upon this season, turning in quality starts in four of his seven starts. Wakefield has 190 wins in his career, 176 of which have been for the Red Sox. Lifetime at Fenway, he is 91-71 with a 4.35 ERA. In his career vs. Oakland, Wakefield is 11-6 with a 4.08 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson, who was activated from the disabled list on Saturday after missing time due to a strained left forearm and elbow tendinitis, put together 5 2/3 shutout innings against the Tigers later in the day, making his first start in more than a month. He allowed just three hits while walking none and striking out four in the 70-pitch effort. A healthy Anderson once again gives the A's a solid five-man rotation, which has officially lost righty Justin Duchscherer (hip) for the season. In three career starts against Boston, Anderson is 2-1 with a 2.05 ERA. Through 22 innings against the Red Sox last year, he tallied 22 strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Tillman will be making his second start this season after assuming the rotation spot vacated, with the move of David Hernandez to the bullpen. The 22-year-old Tillman pitched admirably in Saturday's no-decision in Toronto, allowing two solo homers to a potent Blue Jays lineup over 5 2/3 innings. Tillman yielded six hits total, walking two and picking up two strikeouts in the Orioles' 5-2 loss. He will be facing the Red Sox for the first time this season and the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: The righty has been Boston's most consistent  starting pitcher this season. Buchholz dazzled against the Royals in his last start, firing seven shutout innings and earning the win. In fact, he has given up two earned runs or fewer in his past four starts. Buchholz made six starts in May, going 5-1 with a 3.08 ERA. Opponents are hitting .250 against him this season. This is Buchholz's first start of the season against the Orioles. In seven career outings against the O's, Buchholz is 4-2 with a 4.21 ERA. And his no-hitter on Sept. 1, 2007, was against the O's.

home_pitcher_note: Guthrie allowed three runs in a 26-pitch first inning at Toronto, battling through six frames and allowing four earned runs on seven hits. The right-hander took sole blame for Sunday's series-finale loss, which was his fifth defeat this season. Still, Guthrie has pitched well for the O's and prior to Sunday's start he had allowed just one earned run in his last three outings. He has struggled against the Red Sox, going 1-5 with a career ERA of 4.72 in 13 games (12 starts).
away_pitcher_note: The power lefty has been dominant in recent weeks. In Lester's last start, he defeated the Royals, giving up four hits and one run over seven innings. In six May starts, Lester went 5-0 with a 1.84 ERA. Lester has given up two earned runs or fewer in seven of his past eight starts. Lester has held opponents to a .195 average on the season. Lester won his only start against the Orioles this season, firing 5 2/3 shutout innings on April 23. Lester has dazzled at Camden Yards throughout his career, going 4-0 with a 2.13 ERA in six starts.

home_pitcher_note: Matusz finally got back on track on Tuesday against the Yankees, but still picked up his sixth loss of the year. He had been struggling in the early innings, allowing four runs in the first frame in back-to-back starts against Texas and Oakland. But against the Yankees, the promising 23-year-old southpaw allowed just one baserunner in the first inning. He pitched 6 2/3 innings, holding New York's hefty bats to just one run on six hits while striking out five. Matusz faced Boston for the first time on April 24, 2010, going six innings and allowing three runs on six hits with four punchouts. He has lost a career-high six straight decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Lackey has been durable in his first season with the Sox, failing to make it past five innings only twice in 11 previous starts. A win against the woebegone Orioles would give the right-hander a three-game winning streak for the first time in 2010. He'll have to cut down on the long balls in Camden Yards, a notorious hitter's park when the weather warms up -- Lackey has allowed a homer in seven starts this season. He's 1-1 against Baltimore in two starts this season, and 9-3 with a 3.17 ERA in 14 career starts vs. the Orioles.

home_pitcher_note: Carmona turned in his best start of the season Wednesday night at Comerica Park. He just so happened to do so on the night Armando Galarraga nearly threw the 21st perfect game in Major League history. Still, take nothing away from Carmona, who allowed just three runs (two earned) on nine hits with no walks over eight innings. It was his first complete game of the season. People will remember the missed call at first base that robbed Galarraga of a perfect game, but it was another mistake on another close play at first that wound up costing Carmona two runs in the eighth. He was in top form against the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: The Red Sox aren't sure which version of Dice-K they're getting since he returned from the disabled list. When he's been his old self, Matsuzaka has been tough to hit, as he was three starts ago, when he allowed one hit and walked four in eight shutout innings against the Indians. When he's struggled, however, Matsuzaka has walked too many hitters, like the eight free passes he issued versus Kansas City on May 27. Most troubling has been the lack of strikeouts. Matsuzaka has fanned more than five only twice in seven games. Luckily, his most recent outing, Wednesday against Oakland, was a seven-strikeout effort in which he got a victory despite yielding 10 hits in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Incredibly, Huff was able to make his next turn in the rotation after getting socked in the head by an Alex Rodriguez line drive in the Bronx on May 29. Unfortunately for Huff, his return against the Tigers on Thursday at Comerica Park did not go to plan. He was not sharp, allowing five runs on six hits with two walks, no strikeouts and a hit batter over three-plus innings. Give Huff credit for his ability to bounce back from what could have been a traumatic experience. But he still needs to improve his execution at the Major League level.
away_pitcher_note: The 18-year-veteran is coming off two poor starts, and his knuckleball better start dipping, darting and missing hitters' bats before he works himself out of the rotation, where he's made three consecutive starts. Against Oakland on Thursday, Wakefield surrendered six runs on eight hits in six innings of a 9-8 loss. Eating up innings does the Red Sox no good if Wakefield can't keep the opposition from scoring. He's experienced a mixed bag against Cleveland in his career, posting a lifetime 11-8 record and 4.23 ERA in 27 appearances, including 22 starts. In his eight starts this season, Wakefield has failed to make it through five innings only once.

home_pitcher_note: Masterson grabbed his first win since Aug. 20, 2009, in his last start against the Chicago White Sox. He struggled with his control, walking six and hitting two more batters, but his only run came off Alexei Ramirez's solo home run. The losing streak had lasted 11 games before he finally got that elusive win. "It felt like Justin took about a 3,000-pound gorilla off his back winning tonight, and it was good for him," Indians manager Manny Acta said. Masterson came up in the Red Sox system, but he has never faced them in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Buchholz has been on a tear since losing to the Yankees on May 8. The right-hander has won each of his last five starts. In his last outing, he dominated the Orioles, giving up five hits and a walk in a shutout victory at Camden Yards. Buchholz fanned just two batters that night, but controlled the game and had 11 runs, giving him way more support than he needed. Buchholz last faced the Indians on October 4, 2009, when he allowed six runs on five hits and two walks in three innings. Buchholz will look to improve upon his performance from that night, when he did not factor into the decision.

home_pitcher_note: Mitch Talbot continued to be one of the best starters for the Indians in his last outing, as he outdueled Jake Peavy for the second consecutive time to earn win No. 7 on the season. On two consecutive starts against the White Sox, Talbot has faced Jake Peavy, and both times he has gotten the win. On Saturday, he went seven innings, only giving up a run on Ramon Castro's RBI single in the fourth inning. Lifetime against the Red Sox, Talbot has just one game, a relief appearance from when he was on the Rays. In that game, he gave up four earned runs over three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lester has not lost in nearly two months. Victorious in his last four starts, the lefty went 6 1/3 scoreless innings against Baltimore for his most recent win. He punched out four hitters that night, scattering four hits and three walks. No one has beaten Lester since he lost to the Rays on April 18. Since then, he has won seven of nine starts, reversing his 0-2 start to the season. Lester compiled a 1-0 record in two starts last season against the Tribe. After taking a no-decision during an April game at Progressive Field in which he gave up five runs on seven hits and three walks, Lester turned in a solid performance in the season's final week, pitching 6 1/3 innings of scoreless, two-hit ball.

home_pitcher_note: The big righty is coming off one of his best starts in a while, when he allowed seven hits and two runs over seven innings against the Orioles. He took a no-decision in a game the Red Sox lost in 11 innings. In six Fenway starts this season, Lackey is 4-1 with a 5.60 ERA. This is his second start of the season against the Phillies. On May 21, he took the loss, giving up six hits and four runs over five innings. Opponents are hitting .296 against Lackey on the season, 32 points above his career average. Lackey has given up four earned runs or more in four of his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer is quietly turning into one of the better stories in the National League in the first half of this season. The 47-year-old wonder threw his second complete game of the season on Saturday and earned his 100th win since turning 40. Only two other pitchers -- Jack Quinn and Phil Niekro -- have done so, and Moyer is making it look pretty easy as of late. He has a 2.83 ERA over his past six starts, and he worked quickly and efficiently against San Diego. His complete game took 99 pitches and just over two hours to finish.

home_pitcher_note: The Japanese right-hander might be settling into a rhythm as he's pitched well in three of his last four starts. Most recently, Matsuzaka fired eight shutout innings, walking two and striking out five in a win over the Indians. This is his second start of the season against the Phillies, and the first one was memorable. That was the night he came four outs away from firing a no-hitter. In that contest, he gave up one run over eight innings, walking two and striking out five. Matsuzaka has pitched four times at Fenway this season, going 3-1 with a 4.56 ERA. Opponents are hitting .228 against him this season.
away_pitcher_note: Blanton has continued to struggle, but he's hoping it's a case of deja vu. He is 1-4 with a 6.07 ERA through seven starts. That is not good, but he was 2-3 with a 7.11 ERA through eight starts last season. Blanton recovered nicely. He went 10-5 with a 3.16 ERA in 23 starts to finish the season, making him one of the most consistent and successful starting pitchers in the National League. Blanton would like to start his turnaround against the Boston Red Sox, a team the Phillies have struggled to beat in Interleague Play.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer achieved quite the milestone in his last start, passing Roger Clemens as the all-time innings leader in Red Sox history. Wakefield has pitched 2,777 innings since coming to Boston in 1995. More importantly to Wakefield, he got the win in that outing, holding the Indians to four hits and one earned run over 7 1/3 innings. This will be Wakefield's fifth start back in the rotation since Josh Beckett went on the disabled list with back woes. Wakefield turned in one of his best starts of the season against the Phillies, pitching eight shutout innings in a May 23 victory. As a starter this season, Wakefield is 2-4 with a 5.37 ERA. Lifetime at Fenway, Wakefield is 91-72 with a 4.37 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels carried a no-hitter into the seventh inning Monday against the San Diego Padres at Citizens Bank. He then allowed back-to-back home runs to Adrian Gonzalez and Scott Hairston, which proved to be too much in a 2-1 loss. Hamels has pitched well this season, especially lately. He is 3-3 with a 3.02 ERA in his past seven starts, a sign that Hamels has turned a corner after a frustrating 2009. The only thing he needs now is a little run support, but every Phillies starter is looking for that these days.

home_pitcher_note: The righty continues to make a push toward a possible All-Star appearance. Even on nights when Buchholz doesn't have his best stuff, he gives the Red Sox a chance to win. Take, for example, his last start, when he gave up three earned runs over seven innings, despite walking four and only striking out one. He took the loss in that one, being outpitched by former teammate Justin Masterson. Buchholz has given up three earned runs or less in his last six starts. He has pitched six times at Fenway this season, going 3-3 with a 3.38 ERA. This will be Buchholz's first career appearance against the D-backs. Opponents are hitting .233 against him this season.
away_pitcher_note: Wednesday against the Braves, Kennedy threw a career-high seven shutout innings, but didn't factor in the game's decision. The D-backs' No. 3 starter allowed just three hits and struck out six, but walked a career-high five. "I'm just glad they didn't come back to bite me," Kennedy said of the free passes, "because five walks is a lot." Kennedy has collected quality starts in each of his previous three outings. The young right-hander hasn't allowed more than three earned runs in a game since April 29. Next on Kennedy's agenda is the Red Sox. Despite his brief Major League stint with the New York Yankees, Kennedy has never opposed the Red Sox.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty had a rare letdown in his last start, as he was unable to hold a 5-0 lead against the Indians. Lester took a no-decision in that one, a game the Red Sox lost in the bottom of the ninth. Hurt by his share of seeing-eye hits, Lester gave up nine hits and six runs over six innings, walking one and striking out eight. Before that, he had allowed two earned runs or less in eight of his last nine starts. In seven Fenway starts this season, Lester is 4-1 with a 3.02 ERA. Opponents are hitting .209 against him. This will be Lester's first career appearance against the D-backs.
away_pitcher_note: Manager A.J. Hinch elected to skip Dontrelle Willis' slot in the rotation at least in part to keep Lopez on his normal rest. On Friday against the St. Louis Cardinals, Lopez yielded five runs on six hits over seven innings. He had retired 16 straight Cardinal batters before allowing Brendan Ryan's three-run home run in the seventh, his final inning. Lopez is now 0-3 over his past five starts, and he hasn't won since May 15. Given his five seasons as a Baltimore Oriole, Lopez has pitched against the Red Sox 26 times (20 starts), compiling a 10-9 record with a 4.53 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The big righty has pitched better his last few starts and is coming off his best outing in a while. In a 12-2 win over the Phillies, Lackey gave up six hits and two runs, walking none and striking out three. He is 3-0 over his past four starts. In seven Fenway starts, Lackey is 5-1 with a 5.10 ERA. Opponents are hitting .291 against him. Lackey has made just one career start against the D-backs, giving up just one unearned run over seven innings in a no-decision. He is a career 18-11 pitcher in June with a 3.38 ERA, his best in any month.
away_pitcher_note: Saturday against his original Major League team, the St. Louis Cardinals, Haren was mostly spot-on. He allowed just two runs on six hits and struck out nine over eight innings. He has pitched eight or more innings in five of his 14 2010 starts. The right-hander won consecutive starts for the first time since April 20 and 26. While he continues to lower his uncharacteristically high ERA (4.61), Haren has also improved his strike-throwing; he's walked a total of two batters in his past five outings. In six career starts against Boston, Haren is 2-3 with a 2.65 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old lefty from Venezuela will make his Major League debut in this one, filling in for the injured Daisuke Matsuzaka. Doubront has certainly earned this start, putting up terrific numbers this season at both Double-A Portland (4-0, 2.51 ERA) and Triple-A Pawtucket (2-1, 1.08 ERA). Doubront impressed the Red Sox in Spring Training, pitching seven shutout innings. Doubront has been in Boston's farm system since 2005. He was signed out of Venezuela on July 12, 2004. He has made 109 career starts in the Minors, going 42-30 with a 3.55 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Monasterios was expected to move out of the rotation with the return of Vicente Padilla from the disabled list. However, Chad Billingsley was sent to the DL, meaning Monasterios will stay and make another start. The 24-year-old native of Venezuela has made 11 appearances as a reliever and five as a starter. In those five starts, he's 2-1 with a 3.97 ERA. Most recently, he picked up his first loss of the year by allowing four runs and seven hits in just 2 2/3 innings.
summary: 2010-06-18 - Los Angeles Dodgers (6) @ Boston Red Sox (10) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The veteran knuckleballer had one bad inning in his last start, and it cost him. Wakefield gave up four runs -- all in the fourth frame -- over 7 1/3 innings in a 5-3 loss to the Phillies. Wakefield has made three starts in June, going 1-2 with a 4.79 ERA. In 10 starts this season, Wakefield is 2-5 with a 5.32 ERA. Uncharacteristically, Wakefield has struggled at Fenway this season, going 0-4 with a 6.86 ERA in eight games, six of them starts. Wakefield has pitched four times against the Dodgers in his career, going 1-2 with a 6.64 ERA. Wakefield hasn't faced former teammate Manny Ramirez since 2000. Lifetime against Wakefield, Ramirez is just 6-for-26 with no homers and one RBI.
away_pitcher_note: Padilla will return to the Dodgers' rotation after nearly two months on the disabled list with an inflamed radial nerve in his pitching arm. He has not pitched since April 22, when Los Angeles lost at Cincinnati, 8-5. He made three rehab starts, and in his final one for Triple-A Albuquerque on Sunday, he allowed six runs and eight hits in 5 2/3 innings.
summary: 2010-06-19 - Los Angeles Dodgers (4) @ Boston Red Sox (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The righty continued his streak of solid pitching in his last start against the Arizona Diamondbacks, going 5 2/3 innings and yielding a team-high ninth win, while giving up only three runs on seven hits. It was his sixth win in his last seven starts, a streak which began on May 14. In that time he has posted an ERA of 1.84 and made a solid case for why he should be included in the talk for a possible All-Star appearance. Sunday's start against the Dodgers will be the first of his career.
away_pitcher_note: Kuroda pitched on both sides of a 2-hour, 24-minute rain delay Tuesday at Cincinnati. He pitched four scoreless innings before the delay and one after, although he had to escape a bases-loaded jam in the fifth. He picked up his first win since May 18 after three losses in four starts. Kuroda has struggled in Interleague Play so far in his career, going 1-5 with a 4.89 ERA in six starts. In one Interleague start this season, Kuroda allowed three runs in six innings against the Tigers and lost on May 23.
summary: 2010-06-20 - Los Angeles Dodgers (0) @ Boston Red Sox (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: In the first game of a series that's a rematch of the 2007 World Series (won by the Red Sox in a sweep), Chacin enters with rough numbers (1-3, 6.17 ERA) at Coors Field. Chacin had no fastball command in his last outing but worked through five innings and held the Twins to two runs, but the Rockies' offense did little and the game was a 2-1 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Lester in his last start against the D-backs continued like he has for much of the season, pitching seven solid innings for the Sox, allowing only four hits and two runs. He also walked only three and struck out seven. The two runs came in the second inning off of a two-run home run by Justin Upton. After that inning, Lester recorded all seven of his strikeouts and blanked the D-backs in the next five. With the win, Lester moved to 8-2 on the year with a 3.13 ERA. Just like his last start against the D-backs, this will be the lefty's first career start against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Jimenez continued his dominance in his outing against the Twins on Thursday. He pitched eight innings and gave up only one run, which came in the last inning of his outing. The Twins got eight hits off the ace, but Jimenez got them to hit into four double plays to end innings. He had four strikeouts and two walks in that start. With the Rockies on the verge of getting swept by the Twins, Jimenez snapped that chance, making his record 10-0 when the Rockies lose the game prior to his start. Jimenez faced Boston in Game 2 of the 2007 World Series in his first full season in the big leagues. He gave up two runs and five walks in 4 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: While nothing was easy for Lackey in his previous start, against the D-backs, like he has done much of the season, the righty kept his team in the game and found a way to win, moving his record to 8-3 with a 4.53 ERA. Lackey gave up three earned runs and eight hits, while striking out five in six innings. Throughout the night though, Lackey continued to struggle with his fastball command and kept his pitch count high almost every inning. Lackey will next face the Colorado Rockies, a team he one start against with a career record of 1-0 and a 3.38 ERA.

home_pitcher_note:
In Colorado's 2-0 win against the Brewers on Friday, Hammel extended his scoreless-innings streak to 25 1/3 in his third straight start of seven or more complete innings without allowing a run. Hammel is 3-0 with a 0.31 ERA in the month of June and, though not racking up the strikeouts in his recent outings, has been the beneficiary of timely Colorado hitting and excellent defense.
Hammel, who pitched for Tampa Bay for parts of three seasons, is 0-2 in his career against the Red Sox with a 5.50 ERA in eight appearances.
away_pitcher_note: Making his return to the starting rotation Thursday against the Colorado Rockies after spending time on the disabled list with a right forearm strain, Matsuzaka is hoping to pick up right where he left off in his last start against the Cleveland Indians back on June 7. He pitched eight strong innings, giving up four hits and no runs, while striking out five. Sox manager Terry Francona said going into the start that Matsuzaka is "feeling really good and checked out fine." The righty is 6-4 in Interleague Play with a 4.01 ERA, but he has never faced the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez is coming off his shortest outing of the season, a 2 2/3-inning, three-run effort at Toronto last Sunday. Sanchez walked five in that game, which the Giants still won, 9-6. San Francisco is 8-6 in Sanchez's starts. Though he has thrown only six quality starts, opponents have hit just .205 off him. Sanchez has excelled at AT&T Park, where he's 4-2 with a 2.32 ERA, with an opponents' average of .190.
away_pitcher_note: Wakefield turned in a solid performance in his last start, giving up five hits and three earned runs over 6 1/3 innings against the Dodgers. He left with the lead, but the bullpen couldn't hold it. The Red Sox went on to win the game on a walkoff hit by Dustin Pedroia. Wakefield has made four starts in June, going 1-2 with a 4.67 ERA. Wakefield has made just one career start at AT&T Park and it came in 2004, when he gave up four hits and seven runs (six earned) over four innings. Wakefield took a no-decision in that one. He is 2-3 with a 6.03 ERA lifetime against the Giants.
summary: 2010-06-25 - Boston Red Sox (4) @ San Francisco Giants (5) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner, the Giants' top pitching prospect, will make his season debut Saturday against the Red Sox. The 20-year-old Bumgarner went 7-1 with a 3.16 ERA in 14 starts this season at Triple-A Fresno. The club's first-round pick in the 2007 First-Year Player Draft, Bumgarner made his Major League debut last season, appearing in four games and starting one. In his lone start on Sept. 8, Bumgarner allowed two runs on five hits in 5 1/3 innings against the Padres.
away_pitcher_note: With his win on Sunday against the Dodgers, Buchholz joined four other pitchers as the only 10-game winners in the Majors this season and continues to make his case for why he should be selected to this year's All-Star Game in Anaheim. While nothing was easy for the righty in the first two innings of Sunday's contest -- the first inning required 30 pitches -- he settled down to pitch 6 2/3 innings of scoreless ball, giving up only three hits and striking out four. He also did not give up a hit from the third through sixth innings. In his past eight starts, Buchholz is 7-1 with a 1.62 ERA. The righty has an overall record of 2-0 with a 2.19 ERA in Interleague Play and has never faced the Giants.
summary: 2010-06-26 - Boston Red Sox (4) @ San Francisco Giants (2) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lincecum has successfully put his May slump behind him by winning his past three starts. He has a 1.64 ERA in that span, a start contrast to the 4.95 ERA he logged in six starts last month. Lincecum, who has never faced the Red Sox, is 5-2 with a 3.13 ERA at AT&T Park. Of his 15 starts this year, 12 have been quality outings. He has recorded 10 strikeouts or more in four outings this year and has pitched 23 such games in his career. Facing tough opponents is nothing new for Lincecum, who has confronted teams with winning records in 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note: The power lefty continues to turn in one solid outing after another. His last start was no different as Lester gave up six hits and one run over six innings against the Rockies. He walked one and struck out six, throwing just 90 pitches. Lester could have gone longer in that start, but manager Terry Francona sent up David Ortiz as a pinch-hitter with the bases loaded. Lester has given up two earned runs or fewer in six of his last seven starts. In seven road starts this season, Lester is 3-2 with a 3.12 ERA. This will be his first career start against the Giants. In his four starts in June, Lester is 2-1 with a 3.20 ERA.
summary: 2010-06-27 - Boston Red Sox (5) @ San Francisco Giants (1) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Lackey left his last start in position to get a win, but Jonathan Papelbon blew the save. It wasn't one of Lackey's best games anyway. He gave up 10 hits and five runs over 6 2/3 innings against the Rockies, walking none and striking out seven. Lackey is 3-0 in June.
away_pitcher_note: Shields pitched well enough to win Wednesday night against the Padres, surrendering four runs on six hits and a walk in seven solid innings, but he gave up two home runs that ultimately made the difference and was called for a balk that changed the momentum.
summary: 2010-06-29 - Tampa Bay Rays (5) @ Boston Red Sox (8) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: The righty was rusty at the outset of his first start back from the disabled list, but after that, he settled down nicely. His overall line was five innings, five hits, two runs, four walks and six strikeouts. Matsuzaka is 2-0 with a 2.29 ERA in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Garza rebounded extremely well from arguably the worst start of his career, a 1 1/3-inning disaster in Miami against the Marlins on June 18, with eight solid innings against the Padres on Thursday afternoon. That was Garza's longest outing since May 21.
summary: 2010-06-30 - Tampa Bay Rays (9) @ Boston Red Sox (4) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: This will be his 201st career start at Fenway, passing Roger Clemens for the all-time record. In his last start, Wakefield gave up 11 hits and four runs (three earned) over seven innings in a 5-4 loss to the Giants. In June, Wakefield went 1-3 with a 4.50 ERA in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Interim manager Juan Samuel said after Bergesen's start on Saturday that he will still make his next start despite giving up five earned runs in four innings to the Nationals. It was his first start since being sent to Triple-A Norfolk after early season struggles.

home_pitcher_note: Lester dominated the Giants Sunday, pitching a complete game and surrendering one run on five hits, while striking out nine. With the win, Lester moved to 9-3 with a 2.86 ERA. His career numbers are superb against the division-rival Orioles, with an 11-0 record and 2.06 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Guthrie snapped a streak of five straight losses and three straight non-quality starts in a no-decision Sunday against the Nationals. He went six innings for the 15th time in 16 starts, allowing three runs on three hits and four walks while fanning four.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey continued his winning ways by using all his pitches against the Rays, throwing seven innings and giving up one run on eight hits. With the win, the righty moved to 9-3 on the year with a 4.46 ERA. In 15 career starts against the Orioles, he is 9-3 with a 3.13 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Matusz pitched well on Tuesday against Oakland, allowing three runs in 6 1/3 innings, but still lost his ninth straight decision. In two career starts against the Red Sox he is 0-0 with a 3.86 ERA. He allowed three runs in six innings in his one start at Fenway.

home_pitcher_note: Garza picked up his ninth win of the season Wednesday night against the Red Sox when he allowed three runs on six hits in seven innings at Fenway Park; Garza had electric stuff throughout the outing. He is 16-10 with a 3.30 ERA in 39 career starts at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Matsuzaka got in trouble early and often against the Rays Wednesday, getting behind hitters for most of the game to take the loss. Yet, Matsuzaka still allowed only three runs in six innings. He will face the Rays again Monday, with A career 2-5 record and 5.10 ERA.
summary: 2010-07-05 - Boston Red Sox (5) @ Tampa Bay Rays (6) (Final)

home_pitcher_note: Niemann allowed three earned runs on six hits in 6 2/3 innings to earn a no-decision against the Twins on Thursday in Minnesota. Niemann is 1-1 with a 6.30 ERA in two career starts against the Red Sox; he is 9-3 with a 2.98 ERA in 23 career appearances at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Doubront will be recalled from Pawtucket to make his second big league start, this time in place of the injured Clay Buchholz. He beat the Dodgers in his June 18 debut, giving up six hits and three earned runs in five innings. He's 7-2 with a 2.45 ERA in the Minors in 2010.
